definition: An instance of a running program managed by the operating system.
The smallest unit of execution within a process that can run concurrently.
The OS method for deciding which process or thread gets to use the CPU next.
The act of saving and restoring CPU state when switching between processes or threads.
A situation where processes are stuck waiting on each other, and none can proceed.
A synchronization mechanism used to control access to shared resources.
A memory management technique that gives an application the illusion of having a large, continuous block of memory.
A virtual memory system that divides memory into fixed-size blocks called pages.
The core part of an OS that manages hardware, resources, and low-level operations.
A request from user-level code to the OS kernel for a service.
A signal to the processor indicating an event that requires immediate attention.
The OS component responsible for organizing and storing files on disks.
Temporarily storing data during input/output operations to improve efficiency.
Moving processes between main memory and disk to free RAM.
Different execution modes (like user mode and kernel mode) that control access to hardware and memory.
